scenario: Cross-check shoe listing photos against their catalog SKU and price.
did: Check each photo against the catalog, confirm the right product and price, and flag mismatches.

agree: No — the second opinion flags it, but on a closer look the concern doesn't hold up.

scenario: Build a hand-mobility progress report for two patients from their chart photos.
did: Read each chart, count functional vs limited areas at both time points, and compute recovery %.
why: No issues found — the patient details, the functional-vs-limited counts at the start and at one year, and the recovery percentage (the change in functional areas over all tracked areas, 37%) all check out against the charts.
agree: No — the second opinion flags it, but on a closer look the concern doesn't hold up.

why: The photo-vs-listing checks all hold up (the ground-level hot tub vs the listed back deck, the dated-cabin claim, the zero tours logged). One small thing — C3 and C12 cover the same photo-attribution point from opposite sides, so they nearly double-score it.

agree: No — the second opinion flags it, but on a closer look the concern doesn't hold up.

why: No issues found — the corrected heights and observation times, the per-day growth (about 0.46 cm/day), and the requirement to point out where his hand-drawn chart doesn't match the photos all check out.
